Neil Owen ran 14.18 into a slight breeze to win the 110mH and then in a second run over the same distance with the wind getting up a little stronger to 1.9mps against ran 13.87.
Coming back from injury, however, was Neil Owen to give us one of only three wins with his 'A' sprint hurdles, the others coming from discus throwers Kevin Brown and Leith Marar.

Another best ever came from Bruce Barton in the 'chase - a whopping 11 seconds we make it - as he settled into the BAL team as a regular but over the sprint barriers we missed Neil Owen who was on British Under-23 international duty.
Neil Owen gave us an expected win in the high hurdles before setting off to Japan with Justin for the World Student Games and it was good to see Max Robertson turning out in the 'highs' as well.

Noel Levy did all that was asked of him in the long hurdle race and Neil Owen was again a class apart in the sprint hurdles but Haroun Korjie never recovered from a terrible 100 metre start and an unfit Kassa Tadesse looked sadly and uncharacteristically unfit in the 10k.

Neil Owen turned in a 'man of the match' performance for an exhibition run in the sprint hurdles. A time of just over 14 secs. is commonplace for him now but it put him some four metres clear of the rest.

Neil Owen came home well clear in the 110 metres hurdles where the Frenchman was only 4th but with some field events to come we needed a cushion.
In the high hurdles, Neil Owen was blown to sub 14 sec effort while Noel Levy gained a fine second spot in the 'B' race for excellent points.
Matt gained some consolation from winning the 'B' high hurdles in a time of 14.08 while Neil Owen was back to his classy best winning the 'A' race with a legal sub 14 effort.

Our six wins came from Geoff Dearman (400m), Jason Lobo (800m), Neil Owen (110mH), Stuart Faben (Javelin) and the sprint relay boys. Ezra Clark had one of his better triple jump competitions gaining second spot and narrowly fouling a 15m plus effort.
In the high hurdles Neil Owen showed impressive form in the A race to finish second while new member Dominic Girdler got his Belgrave career off to an exciting start with a fine win in the B event.
In the short hurdles Neil Owen was close to beating Commonwealth bound Damian Greaves while Dominic Girdler ensured more good points with a B win.
Maximum points from Neil Owen and Richard Sear in the sprint hurdles plus a second place in the sprint relay and a win in the long relay moved us into an unassailable lead.
